title: n8n cannot be counted as open source in a tender that requires it
content:
`LICENSE.md` states: *"You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for non-commercial or personal use. You may distribute the software or provide it to others only if you do so free of charge for non-commercial purposes."* Source files containing `.ee.` are separately excluded and require a commercial Enterprise licence.

GitHub's licence detector returns `NOASSERTION` — not a recognised SPDX or OSI licence. n8n is consistent and honest about this, describing itself as *"fair-code"* and *"source available"*, never as open source; faircode.io states plainly that *"Fair-code is not a software license."*

The consequence is procedural, not moral. Any EU or German tender that requires OSI-approved open source cannot count n8n, regardless of the fact that the source is readable and self-hosting is permitted. A second and sharper question — whether a public body running n8n as a cost-recharged shared service for municipalities collides with the prohibition on "hosting n8n and charging people money to access it" — needs legal advice rather than a technical reading.
description: The Sustainable Use License restricts use to internal business purposes and GitHub's detector returns NOASSERTION, so procurement rules demanding OSI-approved licensing exclude it.
